title: Macroeconomics
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/0/title: What does a central bank do?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/0/body: A **central bank** (like the US Federal Reserve or the European Central Bank) sets **interest rates** to try to control inflation and keep the economy balanced. When inflation is high, it usually **raises** rates, and when the economy is weak, it usually **cuts** them.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/1/body: Higher interest rates usually attract money to a currency, because its deposits and bonds pay more. So the currency **tends to strengthen**. This is a **tendency, not a rule**; market expectations play a big part too.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/2/prompt: The Fed made a surprise rate hike. How does the US dollar usually react?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/2/explan: A higher rate means a better return for holding dollars. Especially when it's a surprise, the dollar usually strengthens. How much is never known in advance.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/3/statem: If the market is already sure rates will rise, the currency may barely react to the hike, or even weaken.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/3/explan: When a decision is fully expected, it's already in the price. Sometimes traders even take profits after the news, and the price moves the other way.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/4/body: The market looks at the **future**. If a decision was expected in advance, it's called **priced in**. What moves the market is **surprise** and changes in the **future path of rates**.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/4/tip: The Fed usually holds 8 scheduled meetings a year. The dates are listed in advance on the economic calendar.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/6/senten: To tame inflation, a central bank usually ___ interest rates, and that usually ___ the country's currency.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/6/explan: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive and bring demand and inflation down. At the same time, they make holding that currency more attractive.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/7/prompt: The Fed raised rates more than expected (highlighted candle). What does this EUR/USD move mean?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/7/option: The dollar got stronger vs. the euro
The euro got stronger vs. the dollar
lessons/fundamental-u1-l1/steps/7/explan: EUR/USD is the price of one euro in dollars. When it falls, each euro takes fewer dollars, so the dollar got stronger. That's the usual reaction to a surprise rate hike.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/0/body: **Inflation** is a general rise in prices. **CPI (Consumer Price Index)** measures the price change of a basket of consumer goods and services and comes out **monthly**. **Core CPI** strips out food and energy, which swing a lot.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/1/title: Why are traders so sensitive to CPI?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/1/body: CPI above expectations means **higher rates, or rates staying high for longer**, are more likely. So the dollar **usually** strengthens, and gold and crypto **usually** come under pressure. CPI below expectations usually does the opposite. These are **tendencies, not rules**.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/1/exampl: Same news for gold and crypto
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/2/prompt: US CPI just came out. What's the more likely reaction in the dollar?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/2/option: It tends to strengthen, since inflation beat expectations
It tends to weaken, since inflation beat expectations
No reaction, since the gap is small
A guaranteed 2% rise by the end of the day
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/2/explan: Hotter-than-expected inflation makes a tougher Fed more likely, which usually helps the dollar. A 0.4 percentage point miss is a big surprise for CPI.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/3/prompt: US CPI came in above expectations. Tap the candle that shows the moment the news came out.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/3/explan: After a calm market, this big bearish candle on several times the usual volume is the reaction to the news: the dollar strengthened and EUR/USD dropped more than 40 pips in that one candle.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/4/body: Big central banks like the Fed and the ECB have an **inflation target of about 2%**. The further inflation is above that target, the more likely a **tougher policy** (higher rates, or for longer).
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/4/tip: The market doesn't just look at the headline number. It reads core CPI closely too.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/5/statem: Core CPI includes food and energy prices too.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/5/explan: Core CPI leaves out exactly food and energy, because they swing a lot. That way, the underlying inflation trend is easier to see.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/6/senten: If CPI comes in ___ than forecast, the market sees higher rates as more likely, and the dollar usually gets ___.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/6/explan: Inflation above expectations means the central bank will probably cut rates later, or even raise them. That usually strengthens the dollar.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/7/prompt: US CPI came in below expectations, and gold jumped with the highlighted candle. What's the likely logic behind this move?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/7/option: Unrelated to the news; just chance
lessons/fundamental-u1-l2/steps/7/explan: Lower-than-expected inflation makes a rate cut more likely. The dollar usually weakens, and gold, which is priced in dollars and pays no interest, becomes more attractive.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/0/body: **NFP (Non-Farm Payrolls)** is the number of jobs added in the US last month, **excluding farm work**. It usually comes out on the **first Friday of each month**, along with the **unemployment rate** and **average hourly earnings**.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/1/body: A strong job market (NFP above expectations, low unemployment, rising wages) means the economy is running hot and the central bank is in no rush to cut rates. So the dollar **usually** strengthens. A weak number usually does the opposite.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/1/exampl: Strong; usually good for the dollar
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/2/prompt: What day does the US NFP report usually come out?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/2/option: The first Friday of each month
The last Monday of each month
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/2/explan: The US jobs report usually comes out on the first Friday of each month, and it's one of the most volatile moments of the month for dollar pairs.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/3/statem: A rising unemployment rate is a sign of a stronger job market.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/3/explan: A higher unemployment rate means more people are looking for work and can't find it. It's a sign of a weakening job market.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/4/prompt: NFP came in far above forecast. What does the highlighted candle on USD/JPY show?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/4/option: The dollar got stronger vs. the yen
The yen got stronger vs. the dollar
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/4/explan: USD/JPY is the price of one dollar in yen. When it rises, each dollar buys more yen: the dollar strengthened after the strong jobs number.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/5/body: Sometimes NFP is strong but **wages** are weak, or earlier months were **revised down**. The first reaction can **reverse within minutes**, which is why many traders wait for the dust to settle.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/5/tip: During NFP, spreads widen and slippage is common. Trade a smaller size or stay out.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/6/senten: The NFP report usually comes out on the ___ of each month, along with the ___ rate.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/6/explan: The jobs report includes NFP, the unemployment rate and hourly earnings. Interest rates are set by the central bank, and inflation is reported in CPI.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/7/prompt: This month's jobs report just came out. Which takeaway makes the most sense?
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/7/option: Strong job market; a stronger dollar is more likely
Weak job market; the dollar will surely fall
The numbers contradict each other and tell you nothing
This report only matters for the stock market
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/7/explan: All three parts beat expectations and point the same way. That means the central bank has no reason to rush a rate cut, and the dollar usually benefits. But it's still "more likely", not certain.
lessons/fundamental-u1-l3/steps/8/pairs/: Share of the workforce without a job
A change to earlier months' numbers
